info.description:
# LUME backend API — end-to-end runnable flow

Generated from the Express routes in `src/routes/*` and the controllers/models behind them (182 routes, 200 requests including error-path variants). Import, fill in the four **collection variables** below, then run the collection **top to bottom** (Collection Runner) against a **development** server and database.

## Quick start
1. Set collection variable **`baseUrl`** (default `http://localhost:3000`; the server's `PORT` defaults to 3000).
2. Set **`staffEmail`** and **`staffPassword`** to an existing **Admin or GM** account on the dev DB (`npm run seed` creates demo accounts — see `scripts/seed/people.js`). No credentials are stored in this file.
3. Run. Folder `01` logs in and stores the JWT in `authToken`; every later request authenticates through the collection-level Bearer auth.

## Authentication
* **Staff (dashboard):** stateless JWT. `POST /api/auth/login` (`{email, password}`) returns `{ token, staff }`. Send `Authorization: Bearer {{authToken}}` on **every `/api/dashboard/*`** route and `GET /api/auth/me`. The middleware re-loads the staff record on each call and returns `403` for inactive accounts. Tokens carry `{staffId, role, propertyId}`, signed HS256 with the server's `JWT_SECRET`, and **no expiry**. Some routes additionally require tier `Admin` / `GM` (`requireTier`) — noted per request.
* **Guests (guest app):** **no authentication at all** on `/api/guests/*`, `/api/checkin/*`, `/api/experiences/*`, `/api/bookings/*`, `/api/payments/*`. The guest's identity is just the `guestId` (Mongo id) or the secret `bookingToken` in the check-in link. Those requests are marked "public" and override the collection auth with *No Auth*.
* `POST /api/auth/login` is therefore the mandatory first call; **its Tests script** sets `authToken`, `staffId`, `staffTier` via `pm.collectionVariables`.

## How the flow chains
Variables are captured by each request's Tests script (`experienceId`, `guestId`, `guestToken`, `stayDocId`, `stayBookingId`, `checkInId`, `expBookingId`, …). Order: **auth → departments/staff → property settings → catalog (experiences, spa, dining, F&B, transport, banners) → guest/stay creation → guest check-in → staff check-in review → guest app discovery → guest bookings → payments → staff-side hub bookings → service requests → notifications → checkout & feedback → analytics → comms → cancellations → teardown.** Each request's description states its **Type** (READ/WRITE), **Auth**, and **Depends on**. Deliberate error-path requests are prefixed "⚠ Error path" and sit at the end of their folder.

**One stay = one Booking ID.** `POST /dashboard/guests` creates the stay; its `bookingId` (`EB-<year>-9NNNN`, generated in a pre-request script so re-runs never collide) is `{{stayBookingId}}` and is used everywhere. Hub bookings link to it through `mainStayBookingId`.

## 🚫 UNTESTED BY DESIGN — five external-service features
These requests are embedded in the collection so the API surface is documented, but they have **NOT been run or verified through this collection**, and nothing here should be read as evidence that they work. Each depends on a live external service or has a real-money / real-email side effect. Their saved example responses are hand-written from the controller code, not captured from real runs. All are **skipped by default** (`pm.execution.skipRequest()`, Postman ≥ 10.18) unless you set the variable shown; each request's description repeats this and names the service to verify against.

| Switch (default `false`) | Verify manually against | Why it is untested | Requests |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enableUploads` | Cloudflare R2 / Cloudinary (+ ffmpeg for video) | uploads real files to storage; ID upload → submit → per-guest review depend on it | 13: Upload gallery image; Upload experience image; Upload experience video; Upload spa image; Upload dining image; Upload dining menu file; Upload category image; Upload dish image; Upload vehicle image; Upload banner image; Upload guest ID (front + optional back); Complete check-in (submit for review); Review one guest's ID |
| `enableRazorpay` | Razorpay | live payment provider, real-money side effect, needs a real Checkout payment | 4: Create Razorpay order; Verify payment; Razorpay webhook; ⚠ Error path — Verify with a forged signature |
| `enableAiChat` | OpenAI | paid API; can create requests/notifications | 1: AI concierge chat (may raise a request) |
| `enableEmailSend` | Resend | sends a real email | 1: Send a test email |
| `enableBulkImport` | LeadSquared / database | external CRM push per row; created ids not returned | 1: Bulk-import guests (CSV/XLSX rows) |

Everything outside this table is intended to be run end to end. Two other gates exist but are **not** untested-by-design: `enableTeardown` (default **true**; set it to `false` to keep the data the run created) and `fbOrderId`, which you must set yourself before "Advance order stage" will run.
A skipped request on older Postman versions will simply run and return the documented error.

## Response envelope
Success: `{ "success": true, "data": …, "count"?: n, "message"?: "…" }`. Failure: `{ "success": false, "message": "…" }`, plus `error` (the raw exception text) on 500s, plus `code` on the staff login errors. Malformed ObjectIds surface as `500` with a Mongoose `CastError` — there is no request-validation layer; validation errors also arrive as 500 (or 400 for experiences).

## ⚠ Routes I was not fully confident how to classify (flagged, not guessed silently)
* **`POST /api/payments/webhook`** — Razorpay-to-server callback; signature is over the *re-serialised* body with the API secret, so it is not reproducible from Postman. Classified WRITE / external.
* **`POST /api/payments/create-order` & `/verify`** — need real Razorpay Checkout output; classified WRITE, gated by `enableRazorpay`.
* **`POST /api/guests/auth`** — named "auth" but issues no token; it is an upsert-by-email that also bumps `totalVisits`. Classified WRITE.
* **`POST /api/guests/chat`** — chat answer *and* conditional ServiceRequest/Notification creation (paid OpenAI call). Classified WRITE.
* **`DELETE` on `/api/experiences/bookings/:id`, `/api/guests/spa/bookings/:id`, `/api/guests/transport/bookings/:id`, `/api/guests/dining/reservations/:id`** — soft-cancels, not deletes. Likewise `DELETE /dashboard/spa/:id` and `/dashboard/banners/:id` (soft, `isActive:false`). Classified WRITE.
* **GETs that write (lazy-create defaults):** `GET /api/guests/transport`, `/dashboard/transport`, `/dashboard/property-settings`, `/dashboard/property-settings/guest-app`, `/dashboard/feedback/settings`, `/dashboard/fb-ordering-settings`. Classified READ (idempotent side effect).
* **Legacy/overlapping:** the whole `/api/bookings/*` router (overlaps `POST /api/experiences/bookings`), `PUT /dashboard/guests/:guestId/review` (superseded by the per-guest check-in review) and `GET /dashboard/analytics` (superseded by `/analytics/overview`, and its check-in block likely no longer matches). I could not tell whether a client still calls them.
* **No creator routes:** nothing in this API creates an `FbOrder` (in-room orders) or a guest `Feedback` review, so those hubs are read/advance-only here.
* **`PUT /dashboard/restaurants/:id/block-dates`** writes `blockedRanges` but the guest availability checks read `blockedDates` — may not actually block anything.
* **`GET /api/checkin/by-guest`** — implemented inline in the route file, not a controller. Classified READ.

## Other things worth knowing (not classification, but you will hit them)
* Every hub booking (guest and staff, all four hubs) now derives `mainStayBookingId` server-side from the stay — a client-sent value is honoured only if it belongs to that guest. **TODO (deferred, tracked in the backend README "Known gaps"):** the legacy `POST /api/bookings/create` (folder 17) still does not set it, so bookings made through it are missing from Stay Activity and the Checkout folio.
* Client-supplied prices are trusted in `POST /experiences/bookings` (`price`), `POST /guests/transport/book` (`amount`) and `POST /payments/create-order` (`amount`); `PUT /api/bookings/:id/payment` can mark any booking paid with no verification.
* Fields written that are missing from the schema (silently dropped): `whatsappOptIn` on guest preferences.
* Server-generated hub refs follow the seed's `<stay ID>-<KIND>-<n>` convention via the shared `src/utils/hubRef.js` (Spa `-SPA-`, Experience `-EXP-`, Transport `-TRN-`, Dining `-DIN-`). A guest with no stay on file gets a non-stay fallback ref (`<KIND>-<timestamp>-<rand>`). Data created by this collection is wiped by the next `npm run seed`.
* The bare test IDs, emails (`@example.com`) and hostnames in the saved examples are illustrative; the JWT/token values shown are placeholders, not real credentials.

item.name: 01 · Staff Authentication
item.description:
Staff-side (dashboard) authentication. **`POST /api/auth/login` is the mandatory first call** — it is the only endpoint that issues a token.

**Mechanism:** stateless JWT (`jsonwebtoken`, HS256, signed with the server's `JWT_SECRET`, payload `{staffId, role, propertyId}`; **no `expiresIn` is set**). Every `/api/dashboard/*` route and `GET /api/auth/me` require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the middleware then re-loads the Staff document and rejects inactive accounts.

The login request's **Tests** script stores `token` in the collection variable `authToken`, so every later request authenticates automatically (collection-level Bearer auth = `{{authToken}}`). Guest-facing routes (`/api/guests/*`, `/api/checkin/*`, `/api/experiences/*`, `/api/bookings/*`, `/api/payments/*`) use **no auth at all**.

Before running: set collection variables `staffEmail` and `staffPassword` (an existing Admin or GM account on your **dev** database).

> ## ⚠ NOT TESTED VIA THIS COLLECTION
>
> **Not tested via this collection; verify manually against Cloudflare R2.**
>
> It uploads a real file to an R2 bucket. It needs R2 credentials configured on the server and a real file selected in Postman. Do not read the presence of this request as evidence that it works. The saved example responses on this request are **hand-written from the controller code, not captured from a real run**.
>
> Skipped by default via `enableUploads`.

**Type:** WRITE (mutates state)
**Auth:** Bearer staff JWT — sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{authToken}}` (collection-level auth)
**Depends on:** Auth (01); storage configured

item.name: 11 · Guest Management (creates the stay)
item.description:
Staff-side guest roster. **`POST /guests` is where a stay is born**: it creates the `Guest`, the linked `Booking` (the stay — its `bookingId` is *the* Booking ID quoted by every other hub), placeholder co-guests, and the `bookingToken` that the guest-app link carries.

Depends on: Auth (01), property settings (04) optional. **Feeds nearly everything after it** — the Tests script stores `guestId`, `guestToken` (bookingToken), `stayDocId` (Booking `_id`), `stayBookingId` (`EB-YYYY-NNNNN`-style human ID) and `guestEmail`.

Booking-ID convention (see backend `CLAUDE.md`): one stay = one `EB-YYYY-NNNNN`. The pre-request script generates a fresh `EB-<year>-9NNNN` so re-runs do not collide with seeded stays or with each other. If you omit `bookingId` the API falls back to a non-conforming `BK-<timestamp>-XXXX` — always send one. Running `npm run seed` wipes this test data.

item.description:
Everything staff do in the Experience, Spa, Dining (F&B) and Transport hubs once guests exist: list bookings, add manual bookings against a stay, mark paid, assign rooms. **Every "Add Booking" is linked to the stay by `mainStayBookingId` (`EB-…`)** — verified through `GET /bookings/lookup` first.

Depends on: Auth (01), a stay (11) and the hub catalog (05–09). Cancellations are in **24**. The final request in this folder reads everything back per stay.

**Hub-booking references:** every hub booking a server creates gets a ref of the form `<stayId>-<SPA|EXP|TRN|DIN>-<n>` (per-stay, per-kind counter), generated by the shared `src/utils/hubRef.js` — identical to the seed script. Staff can still type their own ref for Experience (`bookingId`) and Dining (`reservationRef`); it is kept as typed. The Stay Activity request asserts the format across every hub.
